Make the existing durable outbox safe for multiple workers and recovery. Keep createOutbox({store,send,now=Date.now,leaseMs=10,baseDelayMs=2,maxDelayMs=32}) with async enqueue(id,payload), runOne(), stats().
The supplied store.transaction(fn) serializes transactions and rolls back when fn throws. Transactions receive a mutable Map of records. send is external and must never be called inside a transaction.
enqueue IDs are arbitrary nonempty strings. Payloads are JSON-compatible objects/arrays/scalars. Snapshot them at enqueue time and before handing to send so caller/sender mutation cannot corrupt storage. JSON-compatible means no undefined, functions, symbols, BigInt, cycles or nonfinite numbers at any depth; invalid inputs must reject without storing anything.
Enqueue with an existing ID is idempotent only when its JSON value is structurally equal (object key order irrelevant, array order significant). A different payload rejects without changing the prior record. Completed IDs retain idempotency. Return true for a newly enqueued ID, false for an equal existing ID.
runOne atomically claims the oldest due record by enqueue order, preserving that order across retries; equal enqueue timestamps do not change FIFO order. A record is due if pending and nextAt <= now, or sending with leaseUntil <= now. If none is due, return false without sending. Otherwise send(payload,{id,attempt}) where attempt starts at 1 and increases for every claim, including lease reclamation.
Two outbox instances sharing a store must never simultaneously claim the same unexpired record. Claim ownership needs fencing: a stale sender completing or rejecting after another worker reclaimed a lease must not alter the new owner's status, attempts, scheduling or payload.
On owned success mark done. On owned failure return to pending, nextAt = failure completion time + min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2**(attempt-1)); do not throw send failures out of runOne. A claimed run returns true even when send fails or becomes stale. Reject store failures normally; a failed claim never calls send. Recovery must work using a fresh outbox instance with the same store.
stats returns {pending,sending,done} counts without mutating records, including expired leases as sending until reclaimed.
Validate constructor options: store.transaction and send and now functions; leaseMs finite > 0, baseDelayMs finite >= 0, maxDelayMs finite >= baseDelayMs. Invalid construction throws TypeError. All public operations must leave transactions atomic and close normally.
Add deterministic tests using injected time, deferred sends, and transaction failure injection. No real sleeps, networking or packages. Keep the store implementation and its transaction contract intact.
